pelage_geometry_and_topology.patch_morphology: Large, dark, polygonal patches with high edge angularity and sharp pixel-level gradients. The spatial area of dark regions significantly exceeds the area of the light negative space, with shapes primarily presenting as irregular hexagons and pentagons.
pelage_geometry_and_topology.corridor_network: Continuous network of narrow, light-pigmented pathways. Junction nodes consist of well-defined three-way and four-way intersections. Pixel thickness of corridors is relatively uniform and thin compared to patch diameter.

dorsal_ridge_profile.edge_serration: A distinct, low-amplitude, high-frequency jagged contour is visible along the upper neck line, representing the mane. The serration becomes less distinct and smoother as it progresses toward the shoulder.
dorsal_ridge_profile.contour_gaps: Multiple structural breaks are visible along the dorsal ridge where external organisms (oxpeckers) are perched, occluding the continuous line of the mane.

other_distinctive_markers: Presence of multiple oxpeckers (Buphagus sp.) clinging to the dorsal ridge and the lateral flank, creating localized visual occlusions of the underlying pelage geometry.
